decisions.reason: The distributed ALCMS control unit is a core extension of the firm's airfield lighting business, and keeping it costs little while it builds on long-lived installed-base projects, so the option stays open.

The air situation display complements the surveillance portfolio and shares its development base, and airport procurement cycles mean its value has not yet resolved, so keeping it at low cost makes sense.
The airport systems training program is a cheap service option tied to installed systems that generates recurring revenue, so there is no reason to abandon it.

The airfield ground lighting course was only mentioned, not given its own page, but it costs little to maintain and supports the core lighting business, so it is worth keeping despite the weak visibility.

The collaboration software fits the firm's integrated, data-driven strategy, and its prospects remain uncertain after the pandemic slump in airports, so the option should be preserved rather than abandoned.
The MLAT system is the flagship of the firm's surveillance direction, and its value can only resolve over long airport tender cycles, so the firm should keep it and keep investing.
